p01.why: A friend declaration must not declare a concept.

p02.why: The attribute appertains to the concept and using it only warns; Clang 18 rejects an attribute after a concept name.

p03.why: A concept's template head must not have a type constraint.

p04.why: Big auto constrains the invented parameter of size and of the lambda, so int passes and char fails; size<double> gives sizeof(double).

p05.why: The lambda has an auto parameter, so it is generic and may have a trailing clause; int satisfies it.

p06.why: -> must be followed by a type constraint, and int is a type.

p07.why: Access is judged where the check happens, inside a member of Box, so t.secret is valid and Peek<Box> is true.

p08.why: A plain function must not have a trailing requires clause.

p09.why: size_of(Box{}) gives 4 and size_of(3) gives 1, so main returns 0.

p10.why: The trailing requires clause comes before the trailing return type.

p11.why: A requires expression body needs at least one requirement.

p12.why: typename T::missing fails, so the later requirement is not substituted and Trap<int> is not instantiated.

p13.why: A concept-id is a bool constant usable as an array bound, a case label, a noexcept operand, and a condition.

p14.why: A non-generic lambda in a default member initializer of a class template may have a trailing clause; Clang and GCC accept, EDG rejects.

p15.why: Derived<int>::get overrides a virtual function and has a trailing clause; Clang and EDG reject, GCC accepts.

p16.why: The deduced return type char does not satisfy Big.

p17.why: A negation in a requires clause needs parentheses.

p18.why: The template template parameter has the same constraint as Box, so Box is a valid argument.

p19.why: A constrained placeholder must not appear in a functional cast.

p20.why: A requires-expression parameter must not have the name of an enclosing template parameter.

p21.why: The concept uses its own name.

p22.why: Each compound requirement checks decltype((E)): int&, int&&, int, Thing&, and double; char fails Big.

p23.why: A concept's template head must not have a requires clause.

p24.why: Pair needs two arguments, so the type constraint Pair gives an invalid argument list.

p25.why: A concept must not be partially specialized.

p26.why: 'a' gives type char, which fails Big, so the template-id is not valid.

p27.why: A call in a requires clause needs parentheses.

p28.why: noexcept fails, so by the rule Trap is not substituted and the concept is false; Clang substitutes the extra argument first and fails the static_assert, GCC and EDG accept.

p29.why: A constrained placeholder in a structured binding is not valid; EDG accepts it.

p30.why: A requires expression is a bool constant inside or outside a template.

p31.why: typename T::tag fails first, so Trap<int> is never substituted.

p32.why: A trailing clause must not follow the declarator of a pointer to function.

p33.why: At namespace scope secret is not accessible, so the requirement fails and Peek<Box> is false.

p34.why: Outside a template, the requirement p.missing() is not valid.

p35.why: Big... checks each element, so count<int, char> is not valid and the simple requirement fails.

p36.why: A comparison in a trailing requires clause needs parentheses.

p37.why: Any has one parameter and gets two arguments.

p38.why: Both clauses constrain the call operator: int passes, char fails Big, Huge fails Small.

p39.why: Parameters make no objects, so deleted members do not matter, and a later parameter can use an earlier one.

p40.why: The trailing clause comes after the trailing return type, and both clauses are satisfied for int.

p41.why: Big auto... constrains each element of the invented pack.

p42.why: A comparison in a requires clause needs parentheses.

p43.why: The requirements are not evaluated, so throw and runtime() just need to be valid.

p44.why: Tagged has run and tag, int has neither.

p45.why: The extra argument typename int::type is not valid, so the requirement fails and the concept is false.

p46.why: (void) means no parameters, and outside a template every compiler finds it true.

p47.why: A trailing ellipsis in the parameters is not valid; GCC accepts it, Clang and EDG reject.

p48.why: The concept uses its own name in a nested requirement.

p49.why: A leading requires clause works on class, function, variable, alias, member templates, and partial specializations.

p50.why: int().size() depends on no template parameter and is not valid, even in an uninstantiated template.

p51.why: A concept must not be explicitly specialized.

p52.why: Counter passes all three; assignment through a const parameter is not valid.

p53.why: noexcept(f()) is true only for the noexcept function pointer.

p54.why: A concept-id is a bool prvalue constant in every context here.

p55.why: decltype(auto) from n gives int, which is not an lvalue reference.

p56.why: The constraint checks only the deduced placeholder: int, int, int, int&, and int&.

p57.why: A trailing clause must not follow the type in a new expression.

p58.why: Each lambda clause constrains the call operator, and attributes after the first clause appertain to the lambda.

p59.why: A function declared at block scope in a function template must not have a trailing clause.

p60.why: The trailing requires clause comes before the trailing return type.

p61.why: A concept can have constant, template, and pack parameters and any logical-or expression.

p62.why: Returning a void expression deduces void, which fails Wide.

p63.why: The requirements are not evaluated, so counter stays 0 and never() needs no definition.

p64.why: A concept must not be defined in a block.

p65.why: A trailing clause must not follow a parameter declarator.

p66.why: A non-generic lambda in a function template may have a trailing clause; Clang and GCC accept, EDG rejects.

p67.why: A concept has one declaration, its definition.

p68.why: Members of a class template and of a class inside one may have trailing clauses.

p69.why: Box<char> fails Wide and Pair<int> fails its default argument, so those type requirements fail.

p70.why: A member of a local class in a function template may have a trailing clause; Clang and GCC accept, EDG rejects.

p71.why: A requires-expression parameter must not have a placeholder type.

p72.why: The default argument is checked only when a template-id uses it.

p73.why: Inside a member, b.secret is accessible and the expression is true; GCC 14 finds it false (Q-0288), so its static_assert fails.

p74.why: A class template specialization is not instantiated by a type requirement, so incomplete and broken classes pass.

p75.why: Each form of type name is valid for Tagged; int has no tag and int& has no pointer type.

p76.why: decltype(auto) must not be a constrained parameter type.

p77.why: The attribute is valid and unused; Clang 18 rejects an attribute after a concept name.

p78.why: With a variadic concept, each check gives it one element, so every One<X> holds.

p79.why: The nested requirement reads a parameter in an evaluated context; Clang 18 gives false, the other compilers reject.

p80.why: Each pack constraint is one atomic constraint; Clang and GCC find the call ambiguous, EDG picks the AB overload.

p81.why: noexcept appears only in a compound requirement.

p82.why: (void) means no parameters; inside a template Clang finds it false and fails the assertion, GCC and EDG accept.

p83.why: A type requirement must not name a keyword type such as int.

p84.why: requires requires is a clause whose operand is a requires expression.

p85.why: 'a' fails Wide, so pick is not viable and no other candidate exists.

p86.why: A member of a plain class must not have a trailing requires clause.

p87.why: A simple requirement checks only that the expression is valid.

p88.why: one<char> fails SameAs<int>, so naming it is not valid and the requirement fails.

p89.why: A concept must not be defined in a class.

p90.why: The parameter types adjust: an array to a pointer and a function to a pointer to function.

p91.why: A constrained placeholder must not appear in a braced functional cast.

p92.why: A concept name before a declarator needs auto or decltype(auto).

p93.why: t.missing() fails first, so by the rule Trap is not substituted; Clang substitutes the extra argument first and fails the static_assert.

p94.why: The parameter has the name of the enclosing template parameter T.

p95.why: A concept must not be explicitly instantiated.

p96.why: The constrained pick is not viable for char, so the other one gives 2.

p97.why: A virtual function must not have a trailing clause; GCC accepts it, Clang and EDG reject.

p98.why: Every operand of && and || is a primary expression.

p99.why: Any takes a type, and 1 is a value.

p100.why: A qualified concept name works as a type constraint and before auto.

p101.why: A friend defined in a class template may have a trailing clause, and int satisfies it.

p102.why: Nested requirements use parameters only in sizeof, and the && short-circuits before T::value.

p103.why: typename int::type is not valid, so the compound requirement fails and Typed<int> is false.

p104.why: The nested requirements use the parameter only in an unevaluated sizeof.

p105.why: int().size() depends on no template parameter even though the expression has a parameter.

p106.why: Box<> uses the default char, which fails Wide.

p107.why: A trailing clause must not follow the declarator of a variable.

p108.why: Positive takes a constant first, so it is not a type concept.

p109.why: The guide is used only when Wide holds: char gets the implicit guide and int the more constrained user guide.

p110.why: Concepts on auto and int packs, and a call in a concept expression, are all valid.

p112.why: Value<'a'> fails Big, so the type requirement fails; Value<3> passes.

p113.why: A function with no return statement deduces void, which fails Wide.

p114.why: Positive is not a type concept.

p115.why: A default argument in a requires-expression parameter is not valid; GCC accepts it, Clang and EDG reject.
